topic: finite-state hidden aging/epigenetic-memory representation under actionwise CLE matching

claims.claim: For the stated ten-state controlled CTMC pair, full-state chemical-Langevin drift b(z,u)=N a(z,u) and covariance A(z,u)=N diag(a(z,u)) N^T coincide exactly for every full state z and every allowed action u.
assumptions: The only hypothesis-dependent generator row is ((X,M)=(2,1), action B).
The rate perturbation is 2 epsilon h over jumps v=(-2,-1,+1,+2), h=(1,-2,+2,-1), with all rates positive.
The allowed action interface selects the listed generator during each pulse.
claims.evidence: The moment-null identities sum(h)=sum(hv)=sum(hv^2)=0 are expanded in the report; the third-moment contrast is -24 epsilon. The numeric code checks every state/action row at a sample point only.
claims.novelty_boundary: An explicit small witness; no general theorem or literature-priority claim. Independent proof review remains open.
claims.costs: A biology-facing verification would require full-state/action-resolved event acquisition; the hidden memory state is not supplied by the visible X reporter.
claims.falsifier: A symbolic nonzero first- or second-moment difference under an admitted state/action, or any violation of the specified propensities, refutes this instance.
claims.next_gate: Independent derivation review and experimental feasibility assessment for state-resolved event measurement.

claims.claim: If initial support is {(0,0),(0,1)} with q0=P(M0=0|X0=0), P and L are contiguous matched pulses of rate a and duration tau_P, and B lasts tau_B, then the four-arm h_X score difference-in-differences is q0 sigma 10 epsilon (1-exp(-a tau_P))(1-exp(-Lambda tau_B))/Lambda before reporter confusion. Under the same initial support, the reversed isolated order B then P has identical endpoint X laws under the two hypotheses.
assumptions: No passive interval separates P/L and B in the closed-form contrast.
P and L have the same completion rate and duration; P loads M=1 and L loads M=0 from (0,0).
The common reference B rates are c_v>0, Lambda=sum_v c_v, and the primed-mode rate is c_v+sigma epsilon h_v.
Baseline founders are standardized to X0=0; q0 may be unknown but must be lower-bounded for uniform finite-budget claims.
claims.evidence: A successful P has probability q0(1-exp(-a tau_P)); the challenge exit rate is Lambda in both modes; the common c dot h_X term cancels and sum h_v^2=10. A calibrated symmetric five-category reporter multiplies the contrast by kappa=1-5 eta/4. Reversing the pulse order gives TV 0 because B is inactive at X=0; the PB endpoint TV is 6 q0 r s_B |epsilon|/Lambda before reporter confusion and kappa times that after the symmetric reporter.
claims.finite_check_path: work/agents/cell_control/cell_aging_memory/CYCLE3_RUN.json; uniformized endpoint laws at q0=1 and q0=0.4; code checks PB and BP endpoint TV at the illustrative point
claims.novelty_boundary: Conditional order-contrast identity for this construction; not a biological effect estimate or adaptive-policy advantage result.
claims.costs: Four independent arms; matched P/L dose; calibrated X reporter; independent memory-specific assay or validated preparation to lower-bound q0; rate/event and viability controls.
claims.falsifier: Under certified positive nuisance lower bounds, a held-out four-arm contrast whose confidence interval excludes the predicted sign/magnitude family, or failure of CLE/action/matched-load constraints, refutes this model instance.
claims.next_gate: Preregister nuisance confidence sets and test this exact contrast on held-out, donor-blocked lineages.

claims.claim: With four independent arms, a score g in [-2,2], and absolute expected DID at least d_min, the sign-error probability is at most exp(-n d_min^2/32) for n founders per arm; a sufficient test-only count is ceil(32 log(1/alpha)/d_min^2) per arm.
assumptions: Founder-level scores are independent across arms and within-arm founders.
The four arm means use equal n and g is bounded in [-2,2].
The supplied d_min lower-bounds the absolute DID after reporter and initial-memory attenuation.
claims.evidence: Hoeffding applied to the signed sum of four independent arm means; the report charges additional calibration and clustering costs separately.
claims.novelty_boundary: Standard concentration bound, not a biological power calculation.
claims.costs: At the illustrative q0=1 parameter point, 33,523 founders per arm (134,092 total) for alpha=.05, before all calibration/control costs. q0,min=.5 multiplies n by four.
claims.falsifier: Dependence/clustering or unbounded scores invalidate this stated bound; estimate effective independent-unit count and score range before using it.
claims.next_gate: Replace the worst-case Hoeffding design by a preregistered variance/power analysis only after pilot data, preserving held-out confirmation.

claims.claim: No-pulse X-only data do not identify q0 in this witness; a positive uniform separation guarantee therefore needs an independently calibrated lower bound on baseline hidden-memory occupancy or a validated preparation assumption.
assumptions: The pre-pulse reporter measures X only and baseline support has X=0.
The hidden bit M does not affect passive X dynamics before intervention in the stated model.
claims.evidence: Both initial latent states emit X=0 and share the passive law, so no-pulse X observation distributions are identical for every q0; the informative four-arm contrast scales linearly with q0.
claims.novelty_boundary: Model-specific observability obstruction; does not assert that biological memory assays are unavailable.
claims.costs: A binary memory calibration assay with symmetric known error zeta has q0 estimation radius sqrt(log(2/alpha)/(2n0))/(1-2zeta), plus independent calibration of zeta.
claims.falsifier: A validated pre-pulse X-only emission or passive-dynamics difference encoding M would violate the premise and may identify q0 from passive data.
claims.next_gate: Specify and validate a sacrificial baseline assay/preparation with known memory-state labels, sensitivity, and error.

claims.claim: The witness does not establish that its hidden coordinate represents chronological age, epigenetic lesion burden, irreversibility, rejuvenation, or cell identity preservation.
assumptions: No biological experiment, raw-data reanalysis, or model fit was performed for this construction.
claims.evidence: The finite-state construction is intentionally operational; clock/reprogramming papers motivate the measurement distinction but supply no mapping from their clock scores to M in this model.
claims.novelty_boundary: No biological extrapolation, clinical recommendation, or natural-mechanism claim.
claims.costs: A biological test requires calibrated orthogonal clocks, direct lesion/function endpoints, lineage and identity measurements, donors, viability controls, and explicit recovery-resolution horizon.
claims.falsifier: This boundary would change only after a validated biological mapping and held-out predictive intervention result; clock-score movement alone is insufficient.
claims.next_gate: Build an experimentally grounded state-space model from lineage-aware pulse/washout data with a preregistered minimum recovery rate.

prior_art.source: Gassiat, Cleynen & Robin (2016), three consecutive observations under full-rank transition and linearly independent emissions, up to label swapping
prior_art.boundary: Does not directly establish identifiability for this action-conditioned pair or the pulse experiment.

prior_art.source: Thorbergsson & Hooker (2012), Fisher-information experimental design for partially observed Markov decision processes
prior_art.boundary: Supports the acquisition-rule template, not a superiority or optimality theorem for this witness.

decisive_next_gate: Independent proof review; then a calibrated, held-out matched P/L pulse-order experiment with baseline q0 assay, reporter orientation, event-resolved rate acquisition, and simultaneous verification of actionwise CLE equivalence. If any positive signal lower bound or state calibration is unavailable, report UNKNOWN.
